d: The positive feedback loop of labor. The presenting part stretches the cervix and vagina, which signals the hypothalamus to release more oxytocin, and that strengthens the contractions.
A cervical score built from dilation, effacement, station, consistency and position. A score of 8 or more predicts a successful induction, and a lower score calls for cervical ripening first.
An antepartum test that adds four ultrasound items (fetal breathing, movement, tone and amniotic fluid volume) to the non-stress test. Each item scores 0 or 2, and 8 to 10 is reassuring.
Upper brachial plexus injury (C5 and C6) from lateral neck traction, often in shoulder dystocia. The arm is adducted and internally rotated with the elbow extended, the waiter's tip posture.
Failure of the myometrium to contract after delivery, which leaves the placental-bed vessels open. It causes most postpartum hemorrhages and is treated first with massage and oxytocin.
Milk ejection triggered by suckling. Oxytocin from the posterior pituitary contracts the myoepithelial cells around the breast alveoli and pushes milk into the ducts.
